rows.etymology: 1007. Pr. pust, pūst, pọ̄st, pušt ‘bed’ derives < OIA prasupti- ‘sleepiness’ (8846) (Pk.) with modern parallels in Nuristani; the same morpheme appears also in Pr. činkˈak pūst, čaṇḍklak pọst etc. with meaning ‘cobweb, spiderweb’ and is put together by Buddruss und Degener with the ‘bed’ allomorphs. However, I suggest that the ‘web’ forms are homonyms and actually derive < OIA prasiti- ‘a net for catching birds’ which cf. with OIA *sitra- ‘tie, string’ (13400) with a modern reflex in S. There seems to be one more reflex of *sitra- in Tor. ṣɛṣ ‘thin rope’ (Lunsford [2001: 18]).
